driver: Each unit's capacity-schedule tier depends on a short-interval, two-component, worst-channel peak that no single operational feed records: the main archive integrates over a coarse window while sub-unit peak registers lack timestamps so short-interval surges must be aggregated by sub-interval correlation rather than coarse coincidence; the second orthogonal component cancels opposite-signed off-peak and on-peak flows in its monthly net register and must be inverted from an impedance drop demeaned against the net total to remove transducer offset; and channel assignments in the master register have drifted from physical reality so each sub-unit's channel must be inferred from common-mode-rejected differential telemetry and summed at the peak hour rather than over annual totals.
driver_concrete: Each substation's 2027-2029 relief schedule tier depends on its peak 15-minute limiting-phase apparent load (MVA), reconstructed by (1) aggregating monthly non-coincident feeder 15-minute excesses onto 60-minute SCADA peaks in correlated quadrature calibrated on two modernized reference substations, (2) inverting peak-hour reactive power from HV/LV bus voltage drop across transformer impedance and LTC taps demeaned against monthly net kVARh, and (3) identifying each single-phase lateral's true physical phase from common-mode-rejected AMI-to-substation voltage differentials rather than stale GIS phase tags.
